title: At the clothing store
goal: Shop for clothes: name colors and sizes, try things on, compare two options, and say no politely without feeling trapped.
bekal: name colors and use them as adjectives
ask for another size and try things on
compare two things with უფრო and -ზე
say no politely and leave without buying

dialogs.title: დიალოგი — A jacket for the winter
dialogs.intro: Nino goes with Ani to buy a jacket. Notice how two things are compared — the -ზე ending shows up again, this time not for places but for "than".

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: I need a jacket, a warm one.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: I don't know… sizes are different in Indonesia.

lines.speaker: გამყიდველი:
lines.id: That's okay. This one's an M. Try it on!
lines.literal: not — bad-to-it. this — M — is. try-on!

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: It's too small. Do you have a bigger one?

lines.speaker: გამყიდველი:
lines.id: Yes. Would you prefer black or blue?

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Blue. Nino, what do you think?

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: The blue one is nicer than the black one. It really suits you!

lines.speaker: გამყიდველი:
lines.id: Two hundred lari. It's on sale now — one hundred sixty.
lines.literal: two-hundred — lari. now — discount-is — hundred — sixty.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: All right, I'll take it. Can I pay by card?

notes: **Comparing: უფრო + adjective, and the -ზე ending for "than".** *ლურჯი შავ**ზე** უკეთესია* — the blue one is better than the black one. ⚠️ Notice the order is the reverse of English: the thing you compare against comes **first**, then the adjective. Literally "blue black-than better-is".
**უკეთესი = better**, a special form of კარგი. Georgian has a few irregular comparatives like this one, just like *good → better* in English. For every other adjective, **უფრო** is all you need.

**გიხდება = "it suits you" (about how you look).** Another reversed verb: მიხდება (it suits me), გიხდება (it suits you), უხდება (it suits him/her). The compliment you'll hear most in stores — and not always sincerely.

**Colors are ordinary adjectives and go in front of the noun**: შავი ქურთუკი (black jacket), წითელი კაბა (red dress). Some colors are made from a thing + **-ფერი** (color): ყავის**ფერი** (brown, "coffee-colored"), ნაცრის**ფერი** (gray, "ash-colored"), ვარდის**ფერი** (pink, "rose-colored").

**რა ზომა გაცვიათ? — literally "what size do you wear?"** A safe answer if you don't know: *არ ვიცი, მოვიზომავ* (I don't know, I'll try it on). Georgia uses European sizes, so if you're used to US or UK sizes, check a conversion chart first.
**ფასდაკლება = sale, discount.** A compound of ფასი (price) + დაკლება (reduction). You'll see it in shop windows as **-30%** or **ფასდაკლება**.

**Saying no politely.** If you decide not to buy, don't just slip away: *მადლობა, ვიფიქრებ* (thanks, I'll think about it) is enough, and no one will chase you. Georgian sellers rarely push; more often it's the opposite — they send you home to think it over.

grammars.title: Colors
after: Notice that **ლურჯი** (dark blue) and **ცისფერი** (light blue, "sky-colored") count as two different colors, not two shades of the same one — the way "red" and "pink" are separate colors in English.

grammars.title: Comparing two things

head: Sentence
Say it
Meaning
rows: This one is bigger than that one
Do you have a cheaper one?

after: **ყველაზე** (literally "than all") forms the superlative: ყველაზე დიდი (biggest), ყველაზე ლამაზი (most beautiful). One word, and that's all of Georgian comparison done.

blocks.title: Seven sentences for a whole trip to the store
items: **უბრალოდ ვათვალიერებ.** (ubralod vatvaliereb) — I'm just looking. (a lifesaver when you first walk in)
**შემიძლია მოვიზომო?** (shemidzlia movizomo) — Can I try it on?
**სად არის საზომი?** (sazomi) — Where's the fitting room?
**უფრო დიდი გაქვთ?** — Do you have a bigger one?
**სხვა ფერი გაქვთ?** — Do you have another color?
**მადლობა, ვიფიქრებ.** — Thanks, I'll think about it.

blocks.text: ⚠️ One thing that sets Georgian stores apart from big chain stores: in small shops and clothing markets, the seller often **follows you** and comments on every item you pick up. It's meant as service, not surveillance. The sentence *უბრალოდ ვათვალიერებ* makes it clear you don't need help yet, and it's almost always respected.

If you prefer modest clothing: covered styles are easy to find in Tbilisi, and **შარფი** (scarves) are sold everywhere, especially as winter approaches. Useful words in the store: *გრძელი ხელი* (grdzeli kheli — long sleeves) and *გრძელი კაბა* (long dress).

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentences in the store.
Put the words in the right order.

items: Do you have a bigger one?
The blue one is nicer than the black one.

თბილი ქურთუკი მჭირდება. — უფრო დიდი გაქვთ? — სხვა ფერი გაქვთ? — ლურჯი შავზე უკეთესია. — ეს ძალიან ძვირია. — მადლობა, ვიფიქრებ.
